m2c/src/m2c/tools/__init__.py -- Patch C05: local tool executors v0 and the
``run_tool`` entry point.

What this package is
--------------------
The code that touches the user's files.  When the server proposes a tool call
(protocol/v1 ``tool_proposed``) and the approval flow allows it, the client
runs it here and sends back a ``tool_result``.  Patch C05 implemented the seven
file and search tools; Patch C07 added the shell tool (``bash``); I02 wires the
device link to ``run_tool``, and C06 turns the user's settings into the
``user_denylist`` argument.  Nothing here reads settings, talks to the network,
or imports ``daemon/``.

    paths.py    the path guard: containment, symlinks, the two-form denylist,
                no-follow opening.  Ported from daemon/path_guard.py.
    files.py    read_file, list_dir, edit_file, write_file, delete_path.
                Ported from daemon/tools.py (the file tools only).
    search.py   glob and grep (a hardened ripgrep wrapper).
    shell.py    bash (Patch C07): a command run with the user's full
                privileges, no sandbox yet.  Read its docstring first.
    __init__.py ``Caps``, ``ToolContext``, ``ToolResult``, the argument table
                and ``run_tool``.

m2c/src/m2c/tools/paths.py -- Patch C05: the path guard and the two-form
denylist for the local tool executors.

Ported from daemon/path_guard.py (MiniMe, 6977ddf) and extended.  The daemon
module is untouched and nothing here imports it; ``assert_safe_root``,
``is_within_root`` and ``assert_within_root`` keep the daemon's names, signatures
and messages (the 14 daemon tests run unchanged against them, see
tests/tools/test_tools_path_guard_port.py).  What C05 adds is everything the
daemon's guard did not need while it only listed and read files:

* a **resolver per intent** (``resolve_for_read`` / ``_write`` / ``_delete``)
  that returns a project-relative path made of *real* components, so the rest
  of the executor never handles a string it has to re-check;
* the **denylist**, in two forms (below);
* **no-follow opening** (``open_dir_chain``, ``open_regular``) that closes the
  gap between "the path was checked" and "the path was opened".

  called ``~``); only the configured root goes through ``expanduser``.

  inside the root -- for reads, writes and deletes alike.  A symlink inside

m2c/src/m2c/tools/search.py -- Patch C05: glob and grep.

Ported from daemon/tools.py (MiniMe, 6977ddf) in spirit only: the daemon had no
search tools, so these are new.  Nothing is imported from ``daemon/``.

glob
----
Pure Python, no subprocess.  The pattern is matched segment by segment against
the paths under the search directory (``*``, ``?``, ``[...]`` per segment, and a
whole segment ``**`` for "any number of directories, including none").  A
pattern without a ``/`` therefore matches the top level only; the "no files
matched" message says so, because that is the mistake models make.  The walk

* never follows a symlinked directory and never enters ``.git``;
* omits every protected entry (hard and user lists) and does not descend into a
  protected directory;
* lists a symlink only if its real target is a regular file inside the project
  that is not protected;
* is capped by entries scanned (``caps.glob_max_walk_entries``) and by time
  (``caps.glob_timeout_s``), and the result is capped by ``max_results``;
* returns a sorted list (plain code-point order of the project-relative path),
  so the same tree gives the same answer every time.

Ignore files are not read (see the patch notes).

----
A wrapper around ripgrep (``rg``), which is an external tool: nothing is
installed and nothing is imported.  The model controls three things: a regular
expression, a path, and a file-name glob.  None of them may become a ripgrep
*option*, so:

* The argument vector is built in

m2c/src/m2c/tools/shell.py -- Patch C07: the shell tool v0 (``bash``).

SECURITY-CRITICAL
-----------------
Patch C11a (the sandbox, ``m2c.sandbox``) changes WHERE the command runs, not how a call
is checked or supervised: when a working sandbox is available the command runs inside
bubblewrap (project writable, ``.git``, ``.m2c`` and shell rc files read-only, an empty
home, no network, its own PID namespace); when it is not, it runs as described below, with
the user's full privileges, and the visible warning says so.  See "The sandbox" at the end
of this docstring.  The rest of this text is C07's and still holds in both cases.

This module runs a command the model proposed, as the user.  Without the sandbox it can
read and write anything the user can, use the network and start other programs; the only
things between the model and the user's account are then the approval flow (C06 decides,
the device runner and the terminal UI ask) and the checks in this file, which exist to make sure that

* nothing runs unless the caller says, explicitly, that it was authorized;
* a policy ``deny`` still wins over that authorization;
* the command cannot outlive its time limit or its cancel handle;
* the command does not inherit the user's credentials from the environment;
* its output cannot flood memory or inject escape codes into the terminal UI.
